title: Best Sam's Club Dehumidifier (2026): Amana, Keystone & More
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers at Sam's Club
dek: Sam's Club keeps a short dehumidifier list. Here's what's on it, what to check before you spend four figures, and the picks we'd actually buy.
description: The best dehumidifier for Sam's Club shoppers: the club's Amana, Keystone and MaxxAir lineup decoded, plus the pump and commercial picks we'd buy instead.
intro: If you're looking for a **dehumidifier at Sam's Club**, the choice is refreshingly short. The club's own dehumidifier page lists three brands: **Amana**, with a 50-pint unit that has a built-in pump; **Keystone**, with a 35-pint model; and **MaxxAir**, with two commercial-grade machines priced well into four figures.

Some buying guides also name Frigidaire and Whynter as Sam's Club brands, but we couldn't find either live on the club's site — and Whynter's own site lists its standalone dehumidifiers as discontinued. Below, we break down what's actually there, the picks we'd buy for each kind of space — including Keystone's pump-equipped 50-pint, a like-for-like alternative to the club's Amana — and why the club price isn't always the best price.
topPicksLead: The **Keystone 50-Pint Pump** is our top pick for Sam's Club shoppers: it matches the club's Amana on capacity, coverage and pump, from the same brand as the club's 35-pint.

products.name: Keystone 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (KSTAD506PG)
pros: Built-in pump drains up to a sink or window
50 pints a day for spaces up to about 4,500 sq ft
Same brand as the club’s 35-pint Keystone
cons: Costs noticeably more than Keystone’s non-pump 50-pint
Pump hose needs periodic checks for kinks
products.whyWeLoveIt: It’s the most useful kind of dehumidifier for the place most people need one: a basement without a convenient floor drain. It matches the club’s Amana AMND501PAW on the specs that matter — 50 pints, about 4,500 sq ft and a built-in pump — and comes from Keystone, the brand behind the club’s 35-pint model.
products.performance: Keystone rates it at 50 pints a day for up to about 4,500 square feet, with a condensate pump that lifts water to a utility sink or out a basement window, plus ENERGY STAR certification and auto-defrost for cool basement air. Keystone units are built by Midea, and Keystone sits in the top predicted-reliability tier of Consumer Reports’ latest brand survey. Midea’s 2016 recall covered units sold from 2003 through 2013, not today’s KSTAD models. More in our [Keystone guide](/best/best-keystone-dehumidifier/).
products.notes: Keystone sells through several major retailers, so compare prices before you buy.

products.name: Keystone 35-Pint Dehumidifier with Electronic Controls
pros: 35 pints a day for up to about 3,000 sq ft
Built by Midea, a major manufacturer
cons: Club pricing history is hard to pin down
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a family room, large bedroom or mildly damp basement with a floor drain, a 35-pint unit is plenty, and this Keystone keeps things straightforward.
products.performance: Keystone rates it at 35 pints a day for up to about 3,000 square feet. It drains into its bucket or through a gravity hose, which works well if there's a floor drain nearby. Keystone units are built by Midea; Midea's large 2016 recall covered older units made between 2003 and 2013, not the current Keystone lineup. See our [Keystone guide](/best/best-keystone-dehumidifier/) for sibling models.

products.name: AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme Dehumidifier
pros: Published ratings: 85 pints/day AHAM, 180 at saturation
Auto-defrost keeps it working down to 36°F
cons: Overkill for an ordinary damp basement
Heavier and louder than a household unit
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you’re drying a flooded space or a very large crawl space, a commercial unit makes sense — but you should see real numbers first. This is the kind of verified commercial machine we’d choose over the club’s MaxxAir units: AlorAir publishes the ratings, the spec sheet and the warranty terms.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 85 pints a day under AHAM conditions (80°F, 60% RH) and up to 180 pints at saturation, with coverage up to roughly 2,300 square feet. Its low-grain-refrigerant (LGR) design keeps pulling water as the space dries, and the condensate pump lifts water 14.7 feet through a 19.6-foot hose, so it can run unattended. Compare it against other options in our [commercial dehumidifier guide](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: How we pick Sam's Club dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't test dehumidifiers in a lab. We checked which models are actually live on Sam's Club's dehumidifier page, then compared each model number against manufacturer specs, listings at other major retailers and the CPSC recall database.

We ranked on capacity, drainage and the strength of the supporting data, and we note where the identical model is commonly sold for less elsewhere — or where a better-documented alternative is the smarter buy.

blocks.text: For most members, the decision really comes down to one question: is there a floor drain within hose reach of where the unit will sit? If not, the Keystone 50-Pint Pump is worth having. If there is, the Keystone 35-Pint does the job in a mid-size space.
Weighing Amana against a pricier specialist brand? Our [Amana vs. Friedrich comparison](/compare/amana-vs-friedrich-dehumidifier/) covers what Friedrich's longer compressor warranty buys.

sections.heading: The brands that don't check out

blocks.text: Frigidaire and Whynter often appear in lists of Sam's Club dehumidifier brands. We couldn't find a live Sam's Club listing for either. Frigidaire's current dehumidifiers sell widely through other retailers, so you won't miss out. Whynter's own site shows its standalone dehumidifier models as discontinued, with no replacement line announced; see our [Whynter guide](/best/best-whynter-dehumidifier/) for details.

items: **Keystone:** included in Midea's 2016 CPSC recall of about 3.4 million dehumidifiers built from 2003 to 2013 and sold under dozens of brand names. That recall doesn't cover the current Keystone lineup.
**Amana:** named in the 2021 CPSC recall of New Widetech-built dehumidifiers. The recalled units used older model-number prefixes that don't match the current AMND501PAW.
**MaxxAir:** we found no CPSC dehumidifier recall on record.

blocks.text: If you're buying a used or open-box unit of any brand, check the model number and manufacture date at CPSC.gov first.

The **Keystone 50-Pint Pump** is our pick for a Sam's Club shopper with a basement: it matches the club's Amana AMND501PAW on capacity, coverage and pump, from the brand behind the club's 35-pint. The **Keystone 35-Pint** is a sensible choice for a large room or a basement with a floor drain. Skip the MaxxAir units unless you can see a real spec sheet; for genuine restoration or very large spaces, the **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** publishes its numbers. For more options, see our [Costco guide](/best/best-costco-dehumidifier/).

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier at Sam's Club?
faqs.a: The club's own list is short: Amana's 50-pint pump model, Keystone's 35-pint and two MaxxAir commercial units. Our top pick for a basement is the Keystone 50-Pint Pump (KSTAD506PG), which matches the Amana's 50-pint capacity, 4,500 sq ft coverage and built-in pump, and comes from the brand behind the club's 35-pint.

faqs.q: What dehumidifier brands does Sam's Club sell?
faqs.a: Its own dehumidifier page currently lists Amana, Keystone and MaxxAir. We couldn't confirm Frigidaire or Whynter as live Sam's Club dehumidifier brands.

faqs.q: Does Sam's Club sell a dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: Yes. The Amana AMND501PAW is a 50-pint dehumidifier with a built-in condensate pump, which lets you drain water up to a sink or out a window instead of emptying a bucket. The Keystone 35-pint model does not have a pump; Keystone's pump-equipped option is the 50-pint KSTAD506PG, our top pick.

faqs.q: Is MaxxAir a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: It's a real brand best known for RV vents and fans. We couldn't find an independent spec sheet or capacity rating for its commercial dehumidifiers, so ask for one before paying commercial prices.

faqs.q: Is the Sam's Club price on the Amana dehumidifier a good deal?
faqs.a: Not always. The same Amana AMND501PAW has often been listed for less at home-improvement retailers, so compare before you buy — and check the Keystone 50-Pint Pump, which has the same capacity, coverage and pump.

faqs.q: Have any Sam's Club dehumidifiers been recalled?
faqs.a: Keystone and Amana both appear in older CPSC recalls, but those recalls cover earlier models, not the current units Sam's Club sells. We found no MaxxAir dehumidifier recall.
